Seasonal Mattress Cleaning Tips for Different Weather Conditions

July 25, 2024

Keeping your mattress clean is important year-round, but various seasons and weather conditions can impact how thoroughly you should be cleaning your mattress protector, memory foam mattress, and other mattress types. Here we provide seasonal mattress cleaning tipsto help you optimize your cleaning routine.

Table of Contents

Spring Mattress Cleaning Tips

The arrival of spring often coincides with more humidity and rainfall depending on your climate. These tips help freshen mattresses after winter months:

  • Dry Out Mattresses:Allow damp mattresses from humid weather to fully air out and dry before remaking beds to prevent mold growth. Consider hiring cleaning services to deep clean and sanitize mattresses.
  • Sanitize Surfaces:Spring is a good time to deep clean mattress surfaces using solutions like hydrogen peroxide, commercial enzyme cleaner, or gentle detergents to kill bacteria.
  • Beat Allergens:Vacuum mattresses and laundered linens to remove dust and dander accumulation from winter and early spring.
  • Air Quality Control:Open windows regularly to improve airflow and air quality within bedrooms. Circulating fresh air helps control humidity and associated mustiness.
  • Inspect for Bed Bugs:Carefully check mattress seams, crevices, and edges for signs of bed bugs like dark spots or reddish stains after prolonged winter isolation indoors.
  • Rotate and Flip:Rotating or flipping mattresses evenly distributes wear and extends longevity. Do this simultaneously while cleaning.

With spring cleaning, thoroughly clean, inspect, sanitize, and care for sheets and mattresses. This prevents the buildup of microbes and allergens as the weather warms.

Summer Mattress Cleaning Tips

The heat and humidity of summer can cause additional wear and tear on mattresses. Here are helpful cleaning tips for summer:

  • Wash Mattress Covers:Launder mattress pads, toppers, and protectors more often to combat sweat, moisture, and related odors from hot weather.
  • Let Air Circulate:Allow bedding to fully dry before remaking beds. Prop mattresses upright against walls to air out and dry moisture between washings.
  • Clean Spills Right Away:Summer drinks, snacks, and other spills should be spot-cleaned immediately with a gentle laundry detergent. Dish soap, hydrogen peroxide, or enzyme cleaners cut grease.
  • Freshen with Baking Soda:Sprinkle baking soda across the mattress surface and let sit for a few hours to naturally absorb odors before vacuuming up. The antibacterial properties are also clean.
  • Beat the Heat:If possible, keep the bedroom cool with air conditioning to prevent excess humidity and sweat that can seep into mattresses from body heat.
  • Encase Mattresses:Waterproof mattress encasement provides extra protection from spills and moisture damage during sweaty summer months.

Pay extra attention to moisture protection and odor removal from mattresses during hot, humid summers.

Autumn Mattress Cleaning Tips

As autumn approaches, dropping temperatures and falling leaves can impact mattress cleaning needs:

  • Dry Out Mattresses:Allow any damp mattresses from humid late-summer months to fully air out and dry before adding warm bedding.
  • Remove Allergens:Vacuum mattresses thoroughly to eliminate dust mite allergens and dead skin cells that accumulate faster when windows stay closed.
  • Freshen Stale Bedding:Launder all bed linens before cooler weather sets in. Wash blankets aired out over the summer before reuse.
  • Air Quality Control:Enjoy fresh autumn air by opening windows regularly to circulate air before colder temps arrive. Let fresh air into bedrooms.
  • Inspect Closely:Scan mattresses closely for any signs of bed bug infestations before moving activities fully indoors for winter.
  • Rotate and Flip:Redistribute body impressions by rotating or flipping the mattress. A thorough vacuum afterward pulls up debris from the summer months.

Autumn is an ideal transitional time to clean mattresses before weeklong indoor living conditions arrive with winter.

Winter Mattress Cleaning Tips

Colder, drier air and closed windows mean mattresses need extra care in winter:

  • Dry Out Mattresses:Allow any damp bedding to fully air dry before bundling under blankets. Rotate and flip foam mattresses to evenly dry all sides.
  • Disinfect Surfaces:Winter months make conditions perfect for bacteria growth when we stay cooped up indoors. Disinfect mattress surfaces with solutions like hydrogen peroxide.
  • Deodorize Regularly:To keep mattresses fresh when frigid temps deter opening windows, deodorize regularly with baking soda or enzyme cleaners.
  • Deep Clean:Since windows stay shut, winter is the perfect time for a deep clean. Shampoo with commercial cleaners according to label instructions.
  • Vacuum Often:Vacuum mattresses weekly to eliminate allergen and dust buildup that accumulates faster during winter isolation indoors.
  • Inspect for Bed Bugs:Closely scan mattresses for signs of bed bugs that can rapidly spread in colder conditions when seeking warmth.

With no cold water and no open windows, winter air quality quickly diminishes. Compensate by actively cleaning and disinfecting mattress interiors.

When to Professionally Clean Mattresses

For routine seasonal cleaning, DIY methods typically suffice. But in some cases, professional mattress cleaning services become the best option:

  • Visible Mold or Mildew:If moisture causes visible mold or mildew, professional remediation is safest for health.
  • Bed Bug Infestation:Severe bed bug infestations often warrant heat treatments by pest control experts to fully eliminate bugs and eggs.
  • Significant Odor Issues:For severe odors from spills, pets, or smoke that DIY cleaners cannot combat, pros have commercial deodorizing methods.
  • Accumulated Allergens or Dust:When excessive dust mites, dander or debris accumulates, pros have tools to deep clean interior mattress layers.
  • Bodily Fluid Stains:Urine, blood, or other bodily fluid stains often require commercial sanitization beyond DIY abilities. Encasements may also be needed.

While regular spot cleaning can handle most clean your mattress and cleaning needs, don’t hesitate to call in the pros for serious infestation, odor, or sanitization issues.

Mattress Cleaning Checklist

Follow this general checklist for seasonal mattress cleanings:

  • Vacuum the entire surface using a brush attachment
  • Spot treat any visible stains and soiled areas
  • Strip bedding and wash all linens and mattress covers
  • Allow the mattress to fully air out
  • Disinfect the entire mattress surface with a cleaning solution
  • Sprinkle baking soda over the mattress, allow to sit, then vacuum
  • Rotate or flip the mattress if needed
  • Air or deodorize the mattress before remaking the bed
  • Carefully inspect for signs of mold, mildew, or bed bugs
  • Repeat the process for all bedrooms in the home

Set reminders on your calendar to refresh mattresses with each change of season. Consistent cleaning improves the sanitization of mattress stains, extends mattress life, and ensures restful sleep.

Conclusion

Proper mattress cleaning tailored to each season optimizes your mattress care. Be sure to vacuum often, promptly treat spills and stains, wash and rotate mattresses, and disinfect surfaces periodically. Professional cleaning services may be needed for serious infestations, odor issues, or bodily fluid contamination. Keep your mattresses fresh and allergen-free year-round so you can breathe easier and sleep soundly in a clean, healthy bed.
